title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1986 'Ateliers' notes, in which Grothendieck builds an axiomatic framework for elementary geometry (figures and their decompositions). Sigma is an ordered structure of 'figures' with Sup, Inf and a complement operation. Fig opt(Sigma) and Fig opt disc(Sigma) appear to be posets of finite 'optimal' and 'optimal discrete' decompositions (families of figures). The relation F << G means G is finer than F.

On the previous page, Lemma 2 handles a single refinement F << G. Set A = {X^0 | X in F} and B = {X^0 | X in G}. Each a in A should split as a = a' v a'', with a' the part covered by elements of B and a'' the remainder. Then {A, B} lies in a Boolean subalgebra of Sigma (stable under Sup, Inf and complement) iff (a) these splittings hold and (b) the enlarged family B^ = B together with the nonzero a'' is 'admissible'. The smallest such Boolean subalgebra is the one generated by B^. An axiom (At-0-VV^2?) was beginning to be stated.

This page:
- It opens with the provisional claim that {A, B} is an admissible family inside Sigma_A.
- Grothendieck then says this is not enough. The axiom must handle an arbitrary 'flag' F_0 << F_1 << ... << F_n in (F, <<). Such a flag gives rise in Sigma = Sigma_A to a similar flag in Fig opt(Sigma). Reading each F_i through its underlying family, it is reinterpreted as a flag A_0 << A_1 << ... << A_n in Fig opt disc(Sigma).
- To state the relevant axiom he generalizes the notion just defined. Definition (completed on p.115): a subset A of Sigma is 'commensurable' (struck/hesitant wording; 'admissible' on the previous page) if A is contained in a sub-structure Sigma' stable under sup, inf and complement which is a Boolean algebra. He stresses this is stronger than pairwise commensurability. A flag is commensurable if the union of the A_i is.
- Lemma 3 (next page) then produces from a flag the 'new parts' A''_i: A''_0 = A_0, and A''_i collects the nonzero a''_i relative to A_{i-1} << A_i. These are claimed to be pairwise disjoint nonzero elements, giving a partition that generates the Boolean algebra.

Purpose: to formulate a finiteness/compatibility axiom ensuring that successive refinements of figures live in a common Boolean algebra of 'pieces'. This is the lattice-theoretic core of a decomposition (scissors-type) calculus for elementary geometry.
errors: The page is a draft. The opening statement is immediately retracted as insufficient ('Ceci n'est pas tout'), and the definition breaks off mid-sentence.

Whether Sigma is orthomodular is not stated. If it were, pairwise compatibility would already imply joint embeddability in a Boolean subalgebra (a classical theorem for orthomodular lattices). So the remark on p.115 that joint commensurability is strictly stronger implicitly assumes a more general (non-orthomodular) Sigma. No error, but the hypothesis is unstated.

ideas.what: A subset of a lattice with complement is 'commensurable' if it lies in a Boolean subalgebra stable under sup, inf and complement; this is strictly stronger than pairwise commensurability.
ideas.modern_name: Joint compatibility / Boolean subalgebra (block) containing a set, in ortholattice and quantum-logic theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff–von Neumann (1936); compatibility theory in orthomodular lattices (Foulis, Holland, Kalmbach)

ideas.what: Reducing a flag of refinements F_0 << ... << F_n to disjoint 'new pieces' A''_i that generate a common Boolean algebra.
ideas.modern_name: Common refinement / partition generated by a chain of finite decompositions; atoms of a finite Boolean algebra

ideas.what: Stating geometric axioms in terms of flags in posets of optimal (discrete) decompositions Fig opt(Sigma) and Fig opt disc(Sigma).
ideas.modern_name: Poset/nerve of decompositions (in the style of a scissors-congruence complex)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'commensurability' of families of figures is exactly the compatibility notion of quantum logic. He explicitly distinguishes joint from pairwise commensurability. This is the dividing line that orthomodularity removes (pairwise compatible implies contained in a block). His flags of decompositions also resemble the posets of Boolean subalgebras later used in topos approaches to quantum theory (Döring–Isham; Heunen–Landsman–Spitters).
missed.quote: les a ∈ A sont "commensurables dans le sens ensembliste" (NB c'est plus fort que d'exiger qu'ils le soient 2:2)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor historical connection: Grothendieck independently arriving at block/compatibility structure in a geometric setting. It is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine lattice-theoretic preparations (Boolean subalgebras generated by compatible families, refinement flags) in an unfinished foundational project on elementary geometry. The project itself is little known, but this page holds no substantive new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Ceci n'est pas vrai[?] : il suffirait[?] on ne pourra[?] traiter' is better read as roughly 'Ceci n'est pas tout : il suffit qu'on puisse traiter le cas d'un "drapeau" quelconque dans (F, <<)'.
The struck/underlined word in the last line before 'de Σ' appears to be 'commensurable' (consistent with p.115), so read 'une partie commensurable de Σ' rather than 'admissible[?]'.
'd'autres interprétations[?]' is likely 'd'ensembles sous-jacents' or similar ('par le biais des structures d'ensembles ... de chacun des F_i'); uncertain.
Flag indices: the image shows F_0 << F_1 << ... << F_n and A_0 << A_1 << ... << A_n (subscript 1 slightly unclear), as transcribed.
